name: Osskar Horchata-Cinnamon Drift
description: A synth-horchata base with cinnamon and a faint rice-milk finish, lightly carbonated and sold in squat aluminum cans. It's the kind of drink that feels like a memory of something warmer.
flavor_profile: Sweet, milky rice and cinnamon upfront, fading into a soft vanilla-adjacent finish with mild carbonation
cultural_context: A Shelf staple sold in corner dispensaries and vending stacks. Osskar is a legacy street brand from the early Milwaukee corridor, beloved by older Tier 1 residents who remember when the formula was richer.
story_hooks: A character finds an old Osskar can with a pre-reformulation formula date — someone has been hoarding the original stock, and it's worth more than it should be.
Osskar's founder recently died and left the brand recipe in a contested will involving three estranged children and a corponation buyout offer.
A Tier 3 food critic wrote a viral piece about Osskar being 'accidentally transcendent' — now gentrification pressure is threatening the Shelf factory that makes it.
